reasons: The cited text imposes a non-compete directly on Customer ('Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory') with undefined scope and a 24-month post-term tail — squarely the walk-away position, so 'deviation' at high severity is correct.

The redline deletes the entire paragraph, which is the minimal edit that reaches the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer); no residual restriction remains and no other obligation is collaterally removed.

Comment is accurate, in the required voice and prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the playbook fallback (single named product, term only, ≤12 months, carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions).

Deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and no open-ended compete restriction on Customer survives; the reference to Section 12.3 is not in the supplied excerpt but is a plausible supporting point that does not affect the validity of the edit.
